 Orders On Main Petition
 1. This is petition filed by the petitioner u/sec. 12 of
Protection Of Women From Domestic Violence Act, 2005. 
 2. By filing this petition the petitioner has sought
various reliefs fallen U/sec. 19, 20 and 22 of Pwdv Act-
2005.
 3. The format as required under the Dv Act is duly filled
up and the same is presented by the petitioner along with
 3
 C.Misc. 129/2018
the affidavit. In the required format, the detail of the
petitioners' case cannot be made out, the same can be gone
through in the evidence let in by the petitioner. Hence,
before considering the reliefs sought for, it becomes just and
necessary to look into the case of the petitioner. 
 4. The petitioner stated that she is legally wedded wife of
the respondent no.1 and the marriage between the petitioner
and the respondent no.1 was solemnized on 17.02.2016 at
Sri. Balaji Samudaya Bhavan, Subramanyanagara,
Bengaluru as per Hindu rites and customs in the presence
of the family members, elders and well wishers. The parents
Bs Divya vs R1 Bharath Mv And Another on 20 April, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24776461/
2

of the petitioner incurred huge amount towards marriage
expenses, which is amounting to Rs.15,00,000/- and at the
time of marriage, the parents of the petitioner has given gold
ornaments such as mangalya chain, ring and earring, totally
worth of Rs.5,00,000/- to the petitioner . The parents of the
petitioner have given a chain, ring and bracelet to the
respondent no.1. Apart from the gold ornaments the
petitioner has also given silver articles to the respondent
 4
 C.Misc. 129/2018
no.1 has demanded by the respondent no.1's parents and
sister.
 5. The petitioner further submits that after the marriage
both the petitioner and first respondent started living
together at their residence in Jp nagar, Bengaluru. The
respondent no.1 family consisting of the mother and three
sisters. Ever since the date of marriage, the petitioner has
been residing at matrimonial home by discharging as dutiful
wife to the first respondent. On the contrary, the first
respondent and his sisters were not co-operating the
petitioner to stay at matrimonial home and the sister-in-
laws were not allowing the petitioner to lead happy married
life with the first respondent. Even though, the first
respondent did not respond and never used to restrict his
sisters to the interfere with the petitioner. After 15 days of
marriage the mother-in-law and the first respondent started
Bs Divya vs R1 Bharath Mv And Another on 20 April, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24776461/
3

scolding and abusing the petitioner in filthy language
without there being any reasons and they were not allowing
the petitioner to do household work and cooking.
 5
 C.Misc. 129/2018
 6. The first respondent and his mother used to demand
the petitioner to bring money in the form of dowry from her
parents to lead their lavish life in the society. However, the
petitioner refused to comply their illegal demands made by
the first respondent and his mother. But, the first
respondent being very cruel in nature, used to harass and
torture the petitioner as per the tunes of his family
members. 
 7 . The petitioner further submits that the petitioner had
to encounter a number of difficulties placed in her way in
the family and had to, at times, face strong opposition for 
her views regarding the family matters . The petitioner was
once shocked to find that one of her silver articles had been
exchanged by the respondent's mother and sister without
the petitioner's knowledge. When the petitioner expressed
dissatisfaction regarding the same, she was forced to leave
the matrimonial home. 
 8. The petitioner further submits that due to harassment
 6
 C.Misc. 129/2018
of the respondents, the petitioner has tolerated all the things
but unable to bend upon the attitude of the respondents. 
Bs Divya vs R1 Bharath Mv And Another on 20 April, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24776461/
4

Later the petitioner has no option except to lodge a
complaint to the Thalaghattapura police station and based
on the complaint, the first respondent has been called to the
police station and advised him to take care of the petitioner. 
But, the first respondent who is adamant in nature, refused
to accept the advise made by the police. Thereafter, a Fir
has been registered in Crime no.137/2018 for the offence
punishable u/sec. 498-A of Ipc and u/sec. 3 & 4 of Dp Act
against the first respondent and his family members and
same is pending for adjudication.
 9. The petitioner further submits that the first
respondent has neglected the petitioner and the first
respondent is also avoiding maintaining the petitioner for
one or the other reasons. The petitioner submits that the
first respondent is an employee of M/s. Edge Verve (Inforsys
Ltd.,), Electronic City and draws a salary of more than
Rs.50,000/- per month and thus he has got sufficient
 7
 C.Misc. 129/2018
source of income, yet is not providing the basic needs of life
to the petitioner. The first respondent being the husband of
the petitioner, it is the bounden duty to maintain the
petitioner by paying monthly Rs.25,000/- towards food,
clothes, shelter and other expenses considering the status of
the first respondent in the society and also it is necessary to
meet the expenses of Rs.30,000/- towards litigation. Hence,
Bs Divya vs R1 Bharath Mv And Another on 20 April, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24776461/
5

this petition.
 10. On service of notice, the respondent has appeared
before court and filed vakalath. The respondent submits that
the marriage of the petitioner and respondent no.1 is
solemnized on 17.02.2016 at Sri. Balaji Samudaya Bhavan,
Subramanya Nagara, Bengaluru as per Hindu rites and
customs in the presence of the family members. At the time
of marriage, the petitioner parents have given Rs.25,000/-
worth clothes and the respondents have also given worth of
Rs.90,000/- and also given 100 grms gold articles. 
 11. The respondent further submits that after the
 8
 C.Misc. 129/2018
engagement, before the marriage the father of the
respondent has expired due to ill health in the month of
November 2015. The family of the respondent was under the
depression, at that point of time, the petitioner parents
forced the respondent family to marry their daughter,
petitioner herein. The respondents agreed the proposal of
the petitioner's parents and requested them to perform
marriage at any temple and the respondents have not forced
the parents of the petitioner to perform marriage in a grand
manner. 
 12 . It is submitted that soon after the marriage the
petitioner came to the matrimonial home to cohabit with the
respondent. During the stay of petitioner in the matrimonial
Bs Divya vs R1 Bharath Mv And Another on 20 April, 2024 
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24776461/
6

home, the petitioner stay alone as per her will and wish and
the petitioner is not mingling with any other members of the
family, she always consuming tablets/pills and more over
she is not interested in this marriage and due to the force of
parents she has given consent to his marriage with this
respondent. More over, the petitioner is hardly stayed in the
 9
 C.Misc. 129/2018
matrimonial home for about 10 days only.
 13. The respondent further submits that petitioner
always intend to go to her parents house without any
reasons. Immediately, after the marriage, she went to
parents house after 10 days and came along with her
parents and her relatives. It is also submitted that the
petitioner's parents used to bring pills/tablets and given to
petitioner once in while and the parents of the petitioner
have not disclosed the real problem/disease of the petitioner
to the respondents family. The respondent's mother without
any option left her and respondent no.1 went to her
daughter's house, who is at Uk during May 2016, with hope
the petitioner and respondent would lead a happy life lived
together happily without any problem. 
 14 . The respondent further submits that soon after
mother-in-law went to Uk, the petitioner came to
matrimonial home and stayed in the matrimonial home
often and often normally she used to stay in the parents
Bs Divya vs R1 Bharath Mv And Another on 20 April, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24776461/
7

 10
 C.Misc. 129/2018
house, it is further submitted that when respondent during
her stay, she is not doing any work in the home i.e., neither
prepared food or any house hold work she used to go to her
parents home without any intimation to respondent. 
 15 . The respondent further submits that during the
month of June 2016, the Doctor of Spandana hospital called
the respondent for counseling while returning from the
hospital the petitioner did not return to the matrimonial
home from the hospital the petitioner went to her parents
directly due to ill health of the petitioner. After came from
hospital, the parents of the petitioner gave complaint against
the respondent. Thereafter, the petitioner came to
matrimonial home and stayed for few days. During that
period also she continued her old habits. At that moment,
the mother of the respondent came from Usa. The petitioner
again started quarreling with her mother-in-law and thrown
the Mangalya sutra and went to her parents house without
any intimation to the respondent. After the said incidence,
the petitioner came to the matrimonial home along with
 11
 C.Misc. 129/2018
police authority and took her belongings (Mangalya chain,
ear rings, ring bangales) from the matrimonial home. From
that day, onwards the petitioner did not visit the
matrimonial home. After few days, the petitioner gave a
Bs Divya vs R1 Bharath Mv And Another on 20 April, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24776461/
8

complaint against the respondent at Vidyaranyapura police
station u/sec. 498-A of Ipc and also at Thalaghatta pura
police station in Cr.no.137/2018 and Cr.no.92/2018 of Ipc. 
Even though there is no jurisdiction only intend to harass
the respondents she has given complaints in different police
stations. 
 16. It is further stated that the respondent no.1 is having
three sisters, one is at Yalahanka, one is at Usa and
another sister Chennai in this regard they have no
responsible/having any interest in this matter. The
petitioner is an Engineering Graduate and presently she is
working in a company and she is getting handsome salary,
she is not eligible for maintenance. Hence, prays to dismiss
the petition. 
 12 
 C.Misc. 129/2018 
 17. Keeping in mind the evidence given by the petitioner
it becomes just and necessary to look into whether the
orders required by the petitioner various reliefs which are
fallen U/Sec. 19, 20 & 22 of Dv Act can be granted. 
 18. The petitioner in support of her case has got
examined herself as Pw.1 and got exhibited documents as 
Exs.P.1 to 13. Exs.P.1 to 3 are photos, Ex.P.4 is Cd, Ex.P.5
is true copies of marriage certificate, Ex.P.6 is Fir, Ex.P.7 is
charge sheet, Ex.P.8 is adhar card, Ex.P.9 is invitation card
and Exs.P.10 & 11 are statements of respondent, Exs.P.12 &
Bs Divya vs R1 Bharath Mv And Another on 20 April, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24776461/
9

13 are relieving letters of petitioner. The respondent
examined himself as Rw.1 and got exhibited Exs.R.1 to
R.19. Exs.R.1 to 5 are medical documents of petitioner,
Ex.R.6 is undertaking letter, Ex.R.7 is true copy of
complaint dtd: 08.12.2016, Exs.R.8 & 9 are true copies of
statements dtd:09.12.2016 and 14.12.2016, Ex.R.10 is true
copy of complaint dtd: 12.03.2018, Ex.R.11 is true copy of
Fir, Ex.R.12 is true copy of order sheet in C.Misc. no.
379/2018, Ex.R.13 is notarized copy of pass book of mother
 13
 C.Misc. 129/2018
of respondent, Ex.R.14 is medical document, Exs.R.15 & 16
are certified copies of main petition and objections in
M.C.No. 3722/2022, Ex.R.17 is certified copy of affidavit of
assets and liabilities, Ex.R.18 is certified copy of
examination-in-chief of petitioner in C.Misc.Petition no.
379/2018, Ex.R.19 is certified copy of order sheet in
C.Misc.no. 356/2020.
 19. Heard both sides and perused the materials placed
on record. The counsel for the respondent filed written
arguments. The counsel for the petitioner cited below
mentioned citations;
 1.W.P.No.22006 of 2022 between Mr.Uday
 Nayak V/s Mrs. Anitha Nayak, Dd dtd:
 24.11.2022.
 2. Crl.P.No.474/2022 between Sri. Satish.
 N. V/s Smt. Ambika.
 3. Crl.R.P.No.659/2017 between Binita 
 Dass V/s uttam Kumar . 
 20 . The points that arise for consideration are:- 
Bs Divya vs R1 Bharath Mv And Another on 20 April, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24776461/
10

 1. Whether the petitioner is entitled
 14
 C.Misc. 129/2018
 for residential order relief as
 contemplated under Sec.19 of Dv
 Act? 
 2. Whether the petitioner is entitled
 for monetary relief as contemplated
 under Sec.20 of Dv Act?
 3. Whether the petitioner is entitled
 for compensation relief as
 contemplated under Sec.22 of Dv
 Act? 
 4. What order? 
 21. The findings to the above points are as follows:-
 Point Nos.1 to 3 - In the Negative
 Point No.4 - As per Final Order, for the
 following:-
 Reasons
 21. Reasoning on Point Nos.1 to 3: Since these points
are interconnected with each other and requires common
appreciation of evidence, hence to avoid repetition of facts
all the points are taken together for common consideration. 
 22. The case of the petitioner is that the respondent has
given mental and physical harassment by demanding
 15
 C.Misc. 129/2018
additional dowry and for grant of permanent
accommodation. The petitioner has sought for various reliefs
which are fallen U/sec. 19, 20 and 22 of Dv Act.
 23. In the affidavit filed by the petitioner along with
Bs Divya vs R1 Bharath Mv And Another on 20 April, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24776461/
11

petition she has stated that the averments made in the
petition are all true and correct. The petitioner has stated
that she was subjected to verbal and emotional abuse and
she was insulted for not bringing additional dowry and she
was also subjected to economic violence by not providing
money for maintaining herself. Further, the petitioner
stated that the respondent and her mother always tortured
the petitioner both mentally and physically by abusing her
in filthy language without any reason and they were not
allowing the petitioner to do household work and cooking. 
The 1st respondent being husband of the petitioner did not
control the illegal acts of the in-laws, who were tried to
dispossess the petitioner from the matrimonial home. 
Thereafter, the respondent has neglected the petitioner and
also avoiding maintaining the petitioner for one or other
 16
 C.Misc. 129/2018
reasons. When the petitioner tried to leave her marital
house, the respondent was not living the petitioner to lead
her own life. But, in the objections, the respondent had
denied all allegations made by the petitioner. Further, the
respondent stated that after the after the engagement, before
the marriage the father of the respondent has expired due to
ill health in the month of November 2015. The family of the
respondent was under the depression, at that point of time,
the petitioner parents forced the respondent family to marry
their daughter, petitioner herein. The respondents agreed
Bs Divya vs R1 Bharath Mv And Another on 20 April, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24776461/
12

the proposal of the petitioner's parents and requested them
to perform marriage at any temple and the respondents have
not forced the parents of the petitioner to perform marriage
in a grand manner.
 24. It is submitted that soon after the marriage the
petitioner came to the matrimonial home to cohabit with the
respondent. During the stay of petitioner in the matrimonial
home, the petitioner stay alone as per her will and wish and
the petitioner is not mingling with any other members of the
 17
 C.Misc. 129/2018
family, she always consuming tablets/pills and more over
she is not interested in this marriage and due to the force of
parents she has given consent to his marriage with this
respondent. More over, the petitioner is hardly stayed in the
matrimonial home for about 10 days only. Without any the
petitioner has filed this petition. 
 25 . Further on perusal of the petition, it can be seen
that the petitioner and respondent are living in shared
household, at that time and at that time the respondent and
her mother have harassed the petitioner emotionally and
mentally by not taking care of her. On the other hand, the
respondent has also filed objections by denying the
allegations of the petitioner leveled against him. Thereafter,
also the respondent had looked after the petitioner with
fulfilling her all necessities with love and affection. 
Bs Divya vs R1 Bharath Mv And Another on 20 April, 2024 
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24776461/
13

 26. No doubt, as per Sec.3 of Dv Act, if at all the
respondent commits any domestic violence as above pleaded
is fully established by the petitioner then definitely the
 18
 C.Misc. 129/2018
petitioner will be entitled for an order of residential orders as
per Sec.19 of Dv Act and mandatory reliefs as contemplated
under Sec.20 of the Act. 
 27. As per Sec.19 of Dv Act while disposing an
application U/sec.12(1) Pwdv Act, a Magistrate, may on
being satisfied that the domestic violence has taken place
can pass residence order restraining the respondent from
dispossessing or in any other manner disturbing the
possession of the petitioner from the shared household. 
 28. In the case on hand, it is the case of the petitioner
that she is residing along with the respondent after the
marriage in the shared house. When in the respondent has
given mental and emotional torture to bring additional
dowry and also he neglected the petitioner for not brining
sufficient dowry. 
 29. On perusal of the pleadings as well as evidence of
both sides, it appears that there is no such domestic
violence caused by the respondent against the petitioner. 
 19 
 C.Misc. 129/2018 
Further, it appears that the petitioner herself has left the
Bs Divya vs R1 Bharath Mv And Another on 20 April, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24776461/
14

matrimonial home by throwing the mangalya suthra and
went to her parents house without giving any intimation to
the respondent. Therefore, the question of granting
residential orders as per Sec.19 of Dv Act cannot be
considered in favour of the petitioner.
 30. With regard to the possession of mandatory reliefs as
contemplated under Sec.20, it becomes just and necessary
for the petitioner to establish the same. 
 31. The fact that both petitioner and the respondent are
wife and husband is not in dispute. When the petitioner has
let in evidence she has stated that subsequent to marriage,
she is residing along with the respondent in the shared
household, in their the respondent intentionally neglected
the petitioner by demanding additional dowry as well as
neglected the petitioner. The said contention had been
categorically denied by the respondent. Further, he stated
that without any reason the petitioner has left the
 20
 C.Misc. 129/2018
matrimonial home. At this stage, no need to act like what
the petitioner stated in her petition.
 32. On the other hand, after service of notice, the
respondent has appeared before the court by filing vakalath
from his counsel and filed objections to the main petition by
denying all averments pleaded by the petitioner in her
Bs Divya vs R1 Bharath Mv And Another on 20 April, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24776461/
15

petition.
 33. The petitioner examined herself as Pw-1 by filing
affidavit of examination-in-chief. In the said examination-in-
chief, she reiterated the averments of the petition. The
counsel for the respondent has cross examined the Pw.1. In
the cross examination, she admitted that the respondent is
taking care of her and there was no any demand for dowry. 
Further, she admitted that she gave undertaking letter
before police on 04.10.2016 as per Ex.R.6. Further, she
admitted that she was residing with respondent in shared
household only for a period of one month between 17.2.2016
to 17.5.2016. It seems that the petitioner was not residing
 21
 C.Misc. 129/2018
with the respondent in shared household, not exceeding one
month. It seems that there was no any domestic violence
caused by the respondent towards the petitioner. The said
admission is very clear that the respondent has not given
any torture to the petitioner in any manner as stated by her
in the petition.
 34. On the other hand, the respondent himself examined
as Rw.1 by filing affidavit in lieu of examination-in-chief and
reiterated the averments of his objections. In the cross
examination, he denied the suggestions made by counsel for
the petitioner and he had not admitted any suggestions of
the petitioner. 
Bs Divya vs R1 Bharath Mv And Another on 20 April, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24776461/
16

 35. On going through the oral and documentary
evidence as well as affidavit of assets liabilities furnished by
both parties, it is clear that the petitioner is working as
Senior Executive E Mail Supports, Aegis Customer
Support's Pvt. Ltd., and getting gross salary of Rs.26,000/-
and net salary of Rs.21,805/-. Looking into the oral and
 22
 C.Misc. 129/2018
documentary evidence by both sides, it clear that there is no
any domestic violence caused by the respondent towards the
petitioner. Further, she is utterly fails to prove her case by
oral and documentary evidence. 
 36. On perusal of the entire pleadings and documents
and oral testimony of the petitioner, it is crystal clear that
the petitioner is legally wedded wife of respondent and both
are living in the shared house under same roof. Further, it is
clear that the respondent has not given any harassment
mentally and physically to the petitioner by demanding
additional dowry. 
 37. It is undisputed that on the date of filing the
petitioner was legal wedded wife of respondent. Further, the
respondent in his objections stated that she is having
sufficient income to lead her life. To this effect the
respondent has not furnished any single document to show
that she is having sufficient income. But, during the course
of cross examination, the petitioner herself admitted that
Bs Divya vs R1 Bharath Mv And Another on 20 April, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24776461/
17

 23
 C.Misc. 129/2018
there was no any demand for dowry. Mere admission is very
clear that the respondent has not caused any domestic
violence against the petitioner as alleged by the petitioner in
her petition. 
 38 . Further, the petitioner is failed to prove the
allegations which are made by her in the petition as well as
in examination in chief in respect of domestic violence
caused by the respondent u/sec. 3 of Pwdv Act.
 The Section 3 in The Protection of Women from
 Domestic Violence Act, 2005 reads as under;
Sec. 3. Definition of domestic violence.--
 For the purposes of this Act, any act, omission or
 commission or conduct of the respondent shall constitute
 domestic violence in case it. 
 (a) harms or injures or endangers the health, safety, life, limb
 or well-being, whether mental or physical, of the aggrieved
 person or tends to do so and includes causing physical abuse,
 sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse and economic
 abuse; or
 (b) harasses, harms, injures or endangers the aggrieved
 person with a view to coerce her or any other person related
 to her to meet any unlawful demand for any dowry or other
 property or valuable security; or
 (c) has the effect of threatening the aggrieved person or any
 person related to her by any conduct mentioned in clause (a)
 or clause (b); or
 24
 C.Misc. 129/2018
 (d) otherwise injures or causes harm, whether physical or
 mental, to the aggrieved person. 
 39. On careful perusal of the above section, it is clear
 that in this case, the respondent has not committed any
 domestic violence against the petitioner as explained
Bs Divya vs R1 Bharath Mv And Another on 20 April, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24776461/
18

 above. On discussing above, if the respondent has not
 committed any domestic violence against the petitioner,
 as contemplated u/sec. 3 of Pwdv Act, the petitioner is
 not entitled for any of the reliefs as prayed by her in the
 petition. Hence, this court answer these point nos.1 to
 3 in the the negative. 
 40. Point No.4: In view of the findings on the above
 point nos.1 to 3 and the reasons stated therein , this court
 proceed to pass the following: -
 Order
The petition filed by the petitioner U/sec. 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence
Act, 2005 is hereby dismissed.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then p ronounced by me in the open court on this the 20th day of April 2024) . 
(Kusuma. V) MMTC-III, Bengaluru.

 27. As per Sec.19 of Dv Act while disposing an
application U/sec.12(1) Pwdv Act, a Magistrate, may on
being satisfied that the domestic violence has taken place
can pass residence order restraining the respondent from
dispossessing or in any other manner disturbing the

When in the respondent has
given mental and emotional torture to bring additional
dowry and also he neglected the petitioner for not brining
sufficient dowry.

 29. On perusal of the pleadings as well as evidence of
both sides, it appears that there is no such domestic
violence caused by the respondent against the petitioner.
Therefore, the question of granting
residential orders as per Sec.19 of Dv Act cannot be
considered in favour of the petitioner.
 30.
With regard to the possession of mandatory reliefs as
contemplated under Sec.20, it becomes just and necessary
for the petitioner to establish the same.
When the petitioner has
let in evidence she has stated that subsequent to marriage,
she is residing along with the respondent in the shared
household, in their the respondent intentionally neglected
the petitioner by demanding additional dowry as well as
neglected the petitioner.

 36. On perusal of the entire pleadings and documents

the petitioner is legally wedded wife of respondent and both

Further, it is
clear that the respondent has not given any harassment

additional dowry.
Mere admission is very
clear that the respondent has not caused any domestic
violence against the petitioner as alleged by the petitioner in

 38 . Further, the petitioner is failed to prove the

 as contemplated u/sec. 3 of Pwdv Act, the petitioner is
 not entitled for any of the reliefs as prayed by her in the
 petition. Hence, this court answer these point nos.1 to
 3 in the the negative.
In view of the findings on the above
 point nos.1 to 3 and the reasons stated therein
, this court
 proceed to pass the following: -
 Order
